Agreement on Promotion and Protection of Investments between Egypt and Saudi Arabia (2010)
Egypt–EU Association Agreement (2004, Trade and Investment Pillar)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 8 of 2015; Executive Regulations issued by the Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (MLTFCU) per Prime Ministerial Decree No. 95 of 2003 (as amended); Law No. 84 of 2002 on the Establishment of Joint Stock Companies, Limited Liability Companies and Partnerships Limited by Shares (the Companies Law) and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 6 of 2003, as amended by Decree No. 2017 of 2020); Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) Regulation No. 41 of 2021 regarding Customer Due Diligence (CDD) and Anti-Money Laundering/Combating the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) Rules for Regulated Financial Institutions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Attested Copy) – to be apostilled if foreign incorporation is relied upon for UBO/security clearance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Office or Notary Public in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Egypt acceded to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention – Law No. 12 of 1992; Apostille applied by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the country of origin) OR Consular Legalization by the Egyptian Embassy if origin country is not a Hague member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport/National ID of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) with 25% or more ownership, control, or exercise of effective management
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport Office / National Civil Registry of the UBO's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if foreign passport) OR Consular Legalization (if the issuing state is not party to the Hague Convention); certified Arabic translation required if not issued in Arabic

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of Address of each UBO (utility bill, bank statement, or notarized residential affidavit)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility authority, licensed financial institution, or local notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; certified Arabic translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent of any corporate UBO (if a UBO is a legal entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the foreign UBO entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; certified Arabic translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal Record Certificate (Clearance) for each UBO, director and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Interior of Egypt (for Egyptian nationals) or competent criminal records authority in the UBO's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; certified Arabic translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for each UBO / shareholder (anti-money laundering provenance check)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or financial institution maintaining the UBO's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For foreign banks: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; for Egyptian banks: direct bank-issued letter with notarization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders, and authorized signatories against the Consolidated List of the UN Security Council (ISIL and Al-Qaida Sanctions List), the Egypt domestic terrorist list issued by the State Security Court (per Law No. 8 of 2015), OFAC SDN list, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, HMT UK Sanctions List, and national criminal registries. The screening is performed via a secure automated COP (Customer Onboarding and CDD) system integrated with the MLTFCU approved compliant databases. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is triggered if any UBO is a Politically Exposed Person (PEP), including foreign PEPs, domestic high-ranking officials, or individuals connected to international organizations, and PEP status must be verified within 14 days of the start of the business relationship per MLTFCU and CBE Rule 41.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) Commercial Registration System – Online Services Portal (https://www.gafi.gov.eg; also accessible via the Digital Egypt platform, https://www.gafi.gov.eg/English/Pages/default.aspx).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Arabic as the primary language; a Latin transliteration (English/French) may be registered as an ancillary name. The name must not be inconsistent with public order or morals, must not conflict with an already registered trade name, and must conform to the principles of the Arabic alphabet and Egyptian civil notary phonetic rules. For foreign founders, the Arabic name must be a phonetic transliteration of the foreign name unless the proposed name is a recognized transliteration of a global brand name. The name must include the legal form suffix 'LLC' (Limited Liability Company) in Arabic ('شركة ذات مسؤولية محدودة') or the English transliteration 'LLC'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives a written notification from GAFI stating the legal basis for rejection (typically conflict with existing trade name, violation of Article 52 of the Companies Law 84 of 2002, or infringement of a registered trademark). The applicant may file an administrative appeal to the GAFI Appeals Committee (Committee for Adjudication of Grievances) within 15 calendar days from the date of rejection notification. The appeal must be submitted in Arabic on the official GAFI grievance form, accompanied by: a memorandum of law (mudhakkara) explaining the grounds of appeal, the original name clearance application receipt, the rejection notice, and any supporting evidence of non-conflicting use (e.g., prior trademark registration, common law use, or a legal opinion from an Egyptian licensed attorney). The Appeals Committee must issue a decision within 30 working days. If the appeal is rejected at the administrative level, the applicant has the right to challenge the decision before the Cairo Court of Administrative Justice (Mahkamat al-Qada al-Idari) within 60 days from the date of rejection notification, pursuant to the Egyptian State Council Law No. 47 of 1972 (as amended). During appeal, a new name with a different trademark may be simultaneously requested; however, the original name reservation is automatically suspended until the final administrative or judicial resolution. Name reservations are non-transferable and may be extended once for an additional 30 days upon payment of the statutory extension fee, provided the original application is still pending and no third-party objection has been registered.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices (serviced offices, executive business centers, or legal address provision services) are generally permitted for LLCs engaged in e-commerce retail provided the virtual office provider holds a valid commercial registry license and the address is a physical street address in Egypt (not a PO Box). The registered address may be the office address of the legal representative / accounting firm, but not a purely digital or mail-forwarding-only address. The company must maintain a physical administrative seat within Egypt where books and records are kept and where process service can be effected. For e-commerce operations without a physical retail storefront, a serviced office in Cairo, Giza, Alexandria, or a Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) location is acceptable. The virtual office must be equipped to receive notifications from GAFI, Tax Authority, and the Social Insurance Authority. The landlord/the provider of the virtual office must issue a notarized rental contract (lease agreement) registered with the local real estate registry or the local municipality, and the contract must be in the company's name. Use of a private residence of the manager is permitted if the municipality does not restrict commercial activities and the lease is amended accordingly.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 25% annual likelihood for the first fiscal year of operation, increasing to 40% if GAFI receives a complaint, if the company exports promotional solar products subject to Ministry of Trade tariff claims, or if the company requests VAT refunds exceeding EGP 1,000,000. The Commercial Registry and Tax Authority may conduct joint unannounced inspections to verify commercial substance, existence of physical premises, and compliance with the stamp duty law. For an e-commerce retailer using a licensed serviced office, the risk is treated as moderate (probability 20-25% in the first 12 months) because the physical address is verifiable and business operations are evidenced by digital records. A physical inspection is virtually certain (90%+ probability) if the company applies for a Solar Products Certification from the Egyptian Organization for Standardization and Quality (EOS) or if the Ministry of Environment requests environmental compliance documentation for the portable lithium batteries.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: GAFI name clearance application fee (commercial registry name search and reservation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory tariff per GAFI fee schedule (Law 84 of 2002, Executive Regulations, Schedule of Fees); market benchmark $25–$50

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: GAFI electronic incorporation filing fee for LLC (including digital issuance of Certificate of Incorporation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory GAFI fee for electronic incorporation of an LLC with a share capital up to EGP 1,000,000; equivalent USD based on prevailing exchange rate; market benchmark $250–$400

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of incorporation deed and company contracts (Arabic language) before Egyptian Notary Public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice – Notary Public Department (Egyptian Notary Public)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary tariff per Article 15 of Law 68 of 1947 (as amended); approximately EGP 1,000–1,500 per certified page; average engagement 2-3 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Arabic translation of foreign founding documents (passports, apostilled certificates, bank references of foreign UBOs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed legal translation office registered with the Ministry of Justice (translator approved by GAFI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per page ($10–$20/page; 6-10 pages typical for apostilled bundle); no statutory fixed fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization fees in foreign countries for UBO documentation and corporate certificate extraction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent Apostille Authority in each origin country (e.g., U.S. Secretary of State, UK FCDO), or Egyptian Embassy / Consulate (if consular legalization)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing per-country fee (e.g., U.S. $15–$30 per apostille; UK £75 per apostille; Egyptian consular legalization $100–$150 per document); estimated at 2 apostilles + 1 consular legalization for non-Hague members

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: GAFI registration of the LLC in the Commercial Registry (commercial registration number and commercial registry extract)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory commercial registry fee per entity; market benchmark $70–$100

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice in the Official Gazette (Al-Waqa'i Al-Masriya) and a daily newspaper (per Law 84/2002 requirement)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian Official Gazette (Government Press) and licensed Arabic-language newspaper
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff of the Egyptian Official Gazette (approximately EGP 2,500), plus newspaper publishing rate; market benchmark $180–$220

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal professional fee for pre-incorporation due diligence, AML/CFT UBO screening report, drafting the MOA and AOA, and name appeal readiness
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian-licensed law firm / corporate due diligence provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for an LLC with 2 UBOs and uncontested name clearance; hourly or fixed fee (6-10 attorney hours at $95–$160/hr)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended (LLC provisions at Articles 102-117); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and Executive Regulations Decree No. 2310 of 2017 (GAFI One-Stop Shop); Consumer Protection Law No. 181 of 2018 for e-commerce retail; Civil Code Book II on contracts.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — One-Stop Shop Units (network of unified national company registration windows).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Contract (or Company Formation Deed) comprising the Memorandum of Association and the Articles of Association of the Limited Liability Company.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies under GAFI One-Stop Shop LLC formation; the capital is freely fixed in the Articles of Association. Cash subscriptions require a certificate of capital deposit issued by a licensed Egyptian bank before notarization; in-kind contributions require independent expert valuation per Companies Law Art. 104; no escrow account is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST: the incorporation of the Company as an Egyptian limited liability company is approved and the subscription of the entire issued share capital by the sole member is accepted as fully paid. RESOLVED SECOND: the registered office of the Company is fixed at the address set out in the articles of association. RESOLVED THIRD: [General Manager's Name] is appointed General Manager and [Legal Representative's Name] is appointed Legal and Compliance Officer, each with full authority to open bank accounts, sign commercial contracts, and attend governmental authorities. RESOLVED FOURTH: all officers are authorized to complete GAFI registration, tax, and social insurance filings and to execute all documents ancillary to the Company's capital formation, taking effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI e-establishment portal account creation and legal name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Online One-Stop Shop platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the GAFI investor portal, complete the investor profile, and submit three alternative Arabic/English transliterated company names with the corporate objective referencing ISIC 4791 direct online retail of solar portable power products. Pay the online reservation fee and download the name approval certificate.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of sole member and authorized signatories
List of three proposed company names with Arabic/English transliteration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, submit two substitute names via the same portal within five working days without re-payment; escalate unjustified refusals to the GAFI Legal Affairs and Investor Grievance Unit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription of share capital and issuance of bank deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian commercial bank (e.g., National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr, or Suez Canal Bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the draft incorporation contract with a freely fixed capital amount, deposit the subscribed cash consideration in the company's future-account at a licensed Egyptian bank, and obtain the certificate of capital deposit naming the LLC. No escrow account is required for cash contributions; foreign currency deposits require a Foreign Currency Account and AML/KYC declarations.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Completed bank AML/KYC forms and source-of-funds declaration
Valid resident or non-resident ID documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the subscription account on AML/KYC grounds, correct the beneficial ownership documentation and involve the bank's Compliance Officer; unresolved refusals may be escalated to the Central Bank of Egypt supervisory complaints channel within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of the incorporation contract before the GAFI notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop integrated Notary Public Office (Cairo headquarters and regional branches)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the GAFI notary; the sole member or attorney-in-fact executes the Arabic-language incorporation contract containing the statutory clauses (name, object, capital, registered office, managers, fiscal year, liquidation). The notary endorses the signatures, embeds the first board resolution, and releases the notarized certified copies.
required_dossiers: Notarized lease contract of the registered office
Passport copies and two personal photos per subscriber
Notarized power of attorney if signing by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial objections (translation or capital wording) are cured by amending the draft and re-executing the signatures the same day; substantive legal objections are resolved by written ministerial interpretive notes under Companies Law Art. 108.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registry registration, incorporation certificate issuance, and statutory governance books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Commercial Registry (integrated with the Ministry of Trade and Industry commercial record system)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized incorporation contract and first board resolution at the GAFI One-Stop Shop; GAFI registers the company in the commercial register, assigns the unified national company number, issues the incorporation certificate, and arranges publication in the official gazette. Issue the sole member's share certificate and open the statutory registers of partners, board resolutions, and general assembly minutes.
required_dossiers: List of managers and designated signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI queries the file, amend and resubmit within five working days; refusal decisions may be administratively appealed to the GAFI Legal Affairs Department within 30 days and to the Administrative Courts within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration (tax card, VAT, payroll withholding, and stamp duties)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — taxpayer services and e-invoicing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 1 with ETA for the income tax card; simultaneously register for VAT under Law 67/2016, payroll withholding under Law 91/2005 Art. 49, and stamp duties; request the consolidated tax card and VAT certificate. Adopt an accounting system acceptable to ETA and set up the board-approved signatory matrix for tax filings and e-invoicing.
required_dossiers: Notarized lease of the registered office
List of managers and their national IDs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: ETA must issue the tax registration within 20 working days; if queried, supply the missing Arabic lease translation and re-file; unjustified delay is appealable to the Internal Tax Appeal Committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social insurance registration, permanent bank account activation, and e-commerce operational readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI); licensed commercial bank; Consumer Protection Agency (CPA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the establishment file with NOSI within 14 days of hiring the first employee and enroll all managers/employees; activate the permanent corporate bank account using the final incorporation certificate and tax card; register the online store in the CPA e-commerce portal and display the commercial registration and tax numbers on the website. Confirm that no sector-specific license applies to direct online retail of portable battery generators under Law 181/2018; obtain the import registration certificate from GOEIC for the solar hardware.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late NOSI registration is cured by paying the statutory fine under Law 148/2019; CPA rejection for missing Arabic privacy policy is cured within 10 days by filing certified translations; GOEIC deficiencies are corrected by updating the product conformity certificates (IEC 62133 / EU PV standard).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry — General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC), Consumer Protection Agency (CPA), and Civil Defense (Fire Safety) Authority; the Industrial Development Authority only if local assembly is added later.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: GOEIC Importer Registration Certificate for solar panels and portable battery generators; Consumer Protection e-commerce registration certificate; Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate for the warehouse/office; Commercial Registry excerpt with ISIC 4791 scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) — Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — Simplified Environmental Assessment (Form B) required for warehouse/storage facilities exceeding 100 m² storing lithium-ion battery packs; pure e-commerce office-only operations with no material battery storage fall under the registration-only list and are effectively exempt from full EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions arise from retail operations; compliance with Law 4/1994 as amended by Law 9/2009 for any backup generator (NOx < 650 mg/Nm³, PM < 50 mg/Nm³); battery waste must be routed only to EEAA-licensed recyclers under Waste Management Law 202/2020; solar panels and batteries must satisfy Egyptian Standard EOS-2384 and IEC 62133; municipal stormwater connection per Law 93/1962.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate for the storage warehouse (fire extinguishers, smoke detectors, emergency exits, and Li-ion-specific suppression) and for the office premises; structural load clearance certificate issued by a licensed engineer for storage racking; Ministry of Manpower occupational safety and health clearance under Labor Law 12/2003; electrical installation conformity certificate for battery storage and testing areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) under the Ministry of Finance; official e-services portal: https://e-taxta.gov.eg. The ETA administers corporate income tax, VAT, stamp duties, and the mandatory e-invoicing/e-receipts platforms. The Egyptian Customs Authority (ECA) handles customs/export clearance through the NAFEZA National Single Window (CargoX platform).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Incorporate the LLC through the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) at the Egyptian Commercial Registry and obtain the commercial register certificate and memorandum of association (foreign ownership is allowed; no minimum capital requirement). Within 30 days of incorporation, register with the ETA to obtain the unified Tax Identification Number (TIN), tax card, and VAT file. Register as an exporter with GOEIC for the Export Card, open an Egyptian bank account for foreign-currency settlement, and onboard the ETA e-invoicing/e-receipt API with a digital signature certificate and production credentials. Foreign shareholders must act through a resident tax agent; all filings are in Arabic.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: The EG_LLC is a resident juridical person under Egyptian law taxed on worldwide taxable income at the 22.5% corporate income tax rate (Income Tax Law 91/2005, as unified by Law 30/2023). No pass-through election exists; profit distributions are not deductible at the entity level and are subject to shareholder-level taxation. Locations inside a Free Zone or the Suez Canal Economic Zone may alternatively qualify for entity-level exemption or preferential tax under Investment Law 72/2017 and Law 83/2002.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or OECD hybrid mismatch elections exist under Egyptian tax law. Available statutory elections include: (i) Free Zone election under Investment Law 72/2017 substituting income tax with an annual charge of 1% on goods entering/leaving the zone; (ii) Suez Canal Economic Zone (SEZ) election under Law 83/2002 offering tax exemptions and customs/VAT deferral per zone regulation; (iii) simplified VAT regime election for small taxpayers; (iv) voluntary VAT registration below the EGP 500,000 threshold to secure export refunds; and (v) investment incentive deduction of up to 50% of capital expenditures. Elections are filed with GAFI/ETA at incorporation and carry a 5-year lock-in period.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 and its Executive Regulations, administered by the ETA.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual value of taxable supplies of goods or services for mandatory VAT registration; a simplified VAT-basis option applies to small taxpayers; exporters may register voluntarily below the threshold to reclaim input VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time fiscal clearance is mandatory for all VAT-registered taxpayers. Structured XML/JSON e-invoices and e-receipts must be digitally signed (PKCS#12/X.509) and transmitted to the ETA central platform via approved REST/SOAP APIs; the ETA returns a unique invoice UUID and an encrypted QR fiscal code (digital stamp) that must be embedded in the invoice/receipt copy. Invoices rejected by ETA clearance give no right to input VAT deduction, zero-rating, or export refunds. B2C e-commerce sales settled through Stripe and Affirm BNPL must produce an e-receipt at the moment of sale. The e-invoice/e-receipt regime is fully mandatory for all ETA-registered taxpayers as of 2024, with blocking of tax files and penalties for non-compliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to exported tangible goods — including portable solar generators and solar panels — where the LLC is VAT-registered, the buyer is a non-resident, title passes to the foreign customer, the goods physically leave Egypt with customs export proof, and settlement is received in foreign currency through the banking system. Services physically performed outside Egypt and services directly connected to exports (international freight and export handling) are likewise 0% rated. Input VAT on inventory, warehousing, and outbound shipping is fully creditable and refundable; the ETA targets issuance of export refunds within 45 days of a complete electronic claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed through the NAFEZA National Single Window and the Egyptian Customs Authority, referencing the ETA-cleared e-invoice UUID and the customs release number
Commercial Invoice in the ETA-validated electronic format bearing the fiscal QR code and invoice UUID
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export of the goods out of Egypt
Packing List and Certificate of Origin (recommended, supporting tariff preference claims)
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by the Egyptian bank confirming foreign-currency export proceeds were credited to the LLC's account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export refund claims are subject to ETA desk audits and document verification within the 5-year reassessment window. If zero-rating is disallowed or documents are found false or fraudulent, the ETA will claw back refunded input VAT, re-assess 14% output VAT on the export sales, levy the statutory monthly late-payment surcharge (2% per month of unpaid tax), and apply evasion penalties of imprisonment for 1-5 years and/or a fine of EGP 20,000-50,000 or the tax amount if higher (VAT Law 67/2016, arts. 45-46). Additional consequences include export card suspension, blocking of the e-invoice/e-receipt clearance file, and blacklisting on the ETA exporter risk matrix.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law), which superseded Law No. 88 of 2003; CBE retains exclusive authority over licensing of banks, FX dealing, capital account transactions, and enforcement of exchange-control and AML/CFT rules for all Egyptian-licensed credit institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a unified flexible exchange-rate regime effective 6 March 2024, with the EGP rate determined by CBE-authorized dealing banks; current-account transactions (imports of solar panels, portable generators, components, logistics and e-commerce service fees) are freely convertible subject to standard import documentation (ACI/Nafeza customs declaration, VAT e-invoice, insurance and freight contracts). Capital-account transactions are convertible but controlled: inbound equity capital is freely admitted under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, registered with GAFI, and credited in foreign currency or EGP to a designated capital account at a CBE-licensed bank; outbound profit and capital repatriation is guaranteed by law, executed at the prevailing market exchange rate after the LLC files audited financial statements, a board capital/repatriation resolution, ETA tax clearance certificates, and CBE-approval via the bank's Form for Foreign Transfers. Practical hurdles include periodic USD liquidity tightness, payment-priority queues, enhanced UBO verification for non-resident shareholders, and the requirement that dividends be paid only from after-tax distributable profits supported by audited accounts and a final tax-clearance certificate; no generalized freeze or surrender requirement applies at present, but banks may defer large remittances pending CBE liquidity requests.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory repatriation deadline: export proceeds from the LLC's non-oil merchandise must be credited to its Egyptian bank account within 90 days from the dated bill of lading, extendable to a maximum of 120 days for certain perishable or project-specific consignments upon prior CBE approval; non-repatriation triggers a cascading penalty regime (0.5% per month on the un-repatriated amount) and automatic suspension of the exporter's bank facilities. Mandatory conversion ratio: since the March 2024 reform the CBE removed the prior surrender obligation (which had peaked at 100% during the 2022–2023 hard-currency crisis); the LLC may now retain 100% of export proceeds in a Foreign Currency Account (EUR, USD, or other permitted currencies) and convert any portion to EGP at the free market dealing rate. All export contracts, invoices, customs declarations, and shipping documents must be reported electronically to the bank under the CBE's periodic export-reporting framework, and an Export Notification (Form 8) must be lodged with the CBE via the handling bank before shipment to validate the inconvertibility-risk cover for the proceeds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for treasury-depository functions. The CBE does not permit offshore digital EMI platforms (for example, Mercury or Airwallex) to act as the LLC's principal holding account for export/trade proceeds because the receipt of foreign currency by an Egyptian resident through a non-CBE-licensed intermediary is treated as an unauthorized FX-channeling transaction under Circular No. 92/2022 and related AML directives, and banks will reject credits originating from such EMIs without a full source-of-funds reconstruction. Offshore EMIs are viable only as an auxiliary payment-collection layer for consumer card/BNPL receivables (Stripe and Affirm route funds through Egypt-licensed PSP partners such as Fawry, Paymob, or eFin, which then settle in EGP), provided daily sweeps to a CBE-licensed settlement account are performed and all merchant-of-record agreements are disclosed to the corporate bank during KYC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for at least one Egyptian-resident director or the general manager who is an authorized signatory on the LLC's bank account; that person must appear in person at the bank branch for biometric capture, document verification, and a KYC interview before account activation. Non-resident UBOs holding 25% or more of the LLC shares cannot be fully remote-opened: they must either appear physically or complete a video-verified interview with an apostilled/certified copy of their passport or national ID, a current utility bill, and a bank reference letter signed within the last three months; the CBE's AML rules additionally require the resident director to confirm the UBO's source of wealth under penalty of personal criminal liability. Remote-only or fully electronic corporate onboarding is not permissible for a new Egyptian LLC that will process cross-border trade, and at least the final authorization sign-off must occur in-branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO ownership opacity caused by non-resident shareholders operating through intermediate offshore holding vehicles or trusts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificate of incumbency and register of directors from each offshore intermediary; full organizational chart with percentage ownership down to natural persons; passport copies and proof of address for each UBO; six months of personal bank statements for each UBO evidencing lawful source of funds; and a notarized declaration of source of wealth and source of funds, plus the GAFI investor registration certificate for the direct Egyptian LLC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk cross-border online sales pattern (multiple high-risk destination countries, elevated refund/chargeback velocity, or card-not-present fraud indicators under FATF e-commerce ML guidance).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/CFT corporate policy and transaction-monitoring procedures; Stripe and Affirm settlement reports for the preceding 12 months; chargeback and dispute register; customer CDD sample files; geo-blocking policy for sanctioned and high-risk jurisdictions; and a third-party sanctions and adverse-media screening log (OFAC, EU, UN lists) evidencing no hits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection (EGP 500,000 to 2,000,000 equivalent) sourced from a non-resident shareholder whose declared income is inconsistent with the contribution size, triggering a 'source of funds' enquiry.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized share-subscription agreement and board minutes approving the capital call; foreign bank transfer confirmation with SWIFT MT103 details; shareholder's employment/sales/profit contracts and three years of audited financial statements; ETA tax clearance certificate; and, if applicable, a certified copy of the shareholder's sale or loan agreement supporting the capital amount.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected round-tripping or invoice mispricing due to supplier payments to Chinese manufacturers in USD with mixed routing through third-party logistics or procurement intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: China-supplier ISIC-aligned commercial contracts and proforma invoices; ACI/Nafeza electronic customs declarations matching shipped HS codes (8507 batteries, 8541 solar cells/panels); transport and insurance certificates; bank-issued import financing/LC documentation; and a verified beneficial-owner and sanctions-screening package for each supplier intermediary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholder must initiate a SWIFT MT103 wire denominated in USD or EUR to the LLC's designated capital-escrow account at a CBE-authorized bank, with purpose code 'G30 — Capital Contribution under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017' and a clear reference to the LLC's GAFI certificate number and commercial-registry number; the receiving bank verifies the memorandum of association, share-allotment resolution, and CBE-issued Economic Operator Code before crediting; the bank then delivers EGP to the operational account at the free-market dealing rate, issuing a foreign-investment credit note to GAFI; the LLC must file the CBE's quarterly liabilities and claims declaration and, for any retained foreign-currency balance, maintain a Foreign Currency Account within the bank's pre-approved holding limit. The bank must also record the transaction in the CBE's electronic system as a capital-account operation, and repatriation of such capital or related dividends ultimately requires a matching outward remittance approval, audited financial statements, and ETA final tax clearance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments for solar panels and portable-power units will flow over three compliant rails: (1) irrevocable documentary Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700), the default rail for any consignment above USD 50,000, opened by the Egyptian bank in favor of the Chinese beneficiary, with terms (CGED or CIF, delivery against shipping documents) aligned to ACI/Nafeza pre-registration and the HS code mapping; (2) direct SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for low-value, frequently shipped spare parts and accessories, requiring the same ACI customs declaration, an import notification, and prior CBE online approval of the foreign-currency allocation; and (3) Commercial LC with 120–180-day usance tenor for working-capital smoothing, carrying deferred payment drawn under the underlying trade and accepted by the Egyptian bank. Consumer-side proceeds from Stripe and Affirm/BNPL flows cannot be booked directly to the LLC's Egyptian account; they must be aggregated by an Egypt-licensed PSP and settled daily in EGP, with the PSP operating as the merchant of record and the LLC maintaining a reconciliation file for CBE reporting. All outbound USD disbursements are capped by the LLC's annual import budget and require the presentation of the unified ETA e-invoice, customs release certificate, and proof of actual goods arrival for the corresponding import entry.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore USD/EGP deliverable FX forwards with tenors up to 360 days, executed only through CBE-authorized dealing banks, used to lock the EGP cost of confirmed import LCs and capital-project payables.

Offshore Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on USD/EGP: permitted for Egyptian corporates only with express CBE notification through an Egyptian intermediary bank, with settlement in USD/EGP at the official central rate; practical usage is limited because the post-March-2024 float has narrowed the NDF-onshore differential.

USD/EGP cross-currency swaps for trade-related debt service or import-financing programs, subject to CBE prior approval and documented economic exposure, and typically offered by international banks with Egyptian branch or correspondent presence.

European-style FX options (USD/EGP put/call) for protecting high-value import LC payables, available as an OTC product from select authorized dealers and requiring a board hedging policy and annual CBE reporting of notional exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Register Renewal and GAFI Company Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Authority, Ministry of Trade and Industry (one-stop-shop via GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days following the commercial-registration anniversary; the commercial-registration certificate is renewed every 5 years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs an incremental renewal surcharge and flags the commercial registration as expired; prolonged default may trigger suspension of the commercial activity record and ultimately administrative strike-off by the Commercial Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Payroll and Withholding Tax Employer Return (Form No. 4)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Payroll Tax Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January following the calendar year concerned, covering salaries, wages, and staff income tax withheld
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of EGP 500 to 5,000 apply; failure to file blocks issuance of tax clearance certificates for employees and may impair the employer's import/export facilitation status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 21) and Self-Assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Corporate Income Tax Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the tax-year end; for calendar-year taxpayers, no later than 30 April of the following year; final tax payment accompanies the return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A monthly delay addition of 2% per month of the unpaid tax accrues from the statutory due date, plus neglect fines up to EGP 50,000; enforcement includes distraint, attachment orders, and revocation of the tax-clearance certificate required for customs, banking, and public procurement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Value Added Tax Reconciliation Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual VAT reconciliation return due by the end of the second month after the tax-year end; monthly VAT returns remain due by the 15th of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines of up to EGP 50,000 apply under VAT Law 67/2016, plus a monthly late-payment addition of 2% on unpaid VAT; persistent default triggers collection by distraint and criminal referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements and General Assembly Minutes Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Companies Services Center
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: General assembly must review and adopt the annual accounts within 3 months after the fiscal year end; adopted audited statements are filed with GAFI in the same month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of up to EGP 10,000 apply under Companies Law 159/1981 as amended; failure to file audited accounts for two consecutive years authorizes GAFI to initiate forced dissolution or administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Confirmation and Ownership Register Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI — Companies Services Center, AML Compliance Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual UBO confirmation submitted concurrently with the GAFI annual accounts filing; any shareholding transfer must be registered and reported within 30 days following the transfer date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of EGP 20,000 to 100,000 apply under AML Law 80/2002 as amended and Companies Law amendment Law 185/2020; repeated default may disqualify managers and suspend GAFI approvals for dividends and capital-reduction operations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all Egyptian LLCs with no small-entity exemption; every LLC must appoint at least one auditor registered in the Egyptian Accountants and Auditors Register to audit and certify the annual financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) issued by the Ministry of Finance, substantially converged with IFRS and mandatory for all LLCs; IFRS is directly accepted for reporting supervised by the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The UBO register must identify the natural-person ultimate owners holding direct or indirect control or 25% or more of ownership, must be updated within 30 days of any shareholding transfer, and an annual confirmation letter signed by the manager(s) and auditor must accompany the GAFI annual accounts filing each fiscal year.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% flat rate on net taxable income of resident juridical persons (Law No. 91 of 2005, Article 5, as amended by Law No. 1 of 2020).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general income-tax holiday applies to the direct online retail of portable solar power equipment under the Investment Law (Law No. 72 of 2017); a retail trading activity is outside the restricted incentive sectors. The effective rate may be modestly reduced by accelerated depreciation on fixed assets, 10% statutory donation cap, and the export-income incentives described in Article 14 of Law No. 91 of 2005 when export documentation is retained. Small taxpayers with annual turnover below EGP 20,000,000 may elect the presumptive tax regime under Law No. 2 of 2023, applying tax scales from 0.1% to 1.5% of turnover, but the election is inapplicable if the LLC is part of a multinational group or fails bookkeeping tests.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return for Legal Persons — Form No. 20, filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal (eta.gov.eg e-tax system).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; advance payment of the estimated tax is made in four quarterly instalments during the fiscal year and credited against the annual assessments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return and audited financial statements must be filed within 4 months of the end of the tax year (Article 46 of Law No. 91 of 2005). For a calendar-year LLC the filing deadline is 30 April; the four instalments are due in the first month of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The unique Egyptian Tax Card identification number of the LLC, together with the separate income tax and VAT file numbers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident LLC enters its Egyptian Tax Card number; non-resident shareholders do not appear in this box and no Egyptian tax card is required for a foreign parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered full legal name, commercial registration (CR) number, head-office address, and principal activity: ISIC 4791, direct online retail of portable battery generators and solar panels.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The LLC must be identified exactly as in the Commercial Register; the non-resident shareholder's name is disclosed only in the shareholder register annexed to the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the tax period, expressed as a full 12-month period; short first or final periods are re-indexed to annual equivalence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent should align the LLC fiscal year with the consolidated IFRS reporting calendar to minimise partial-period reconciliations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross sales value of solar generators, solar panels, and accessories delivered through Stripe, Affirm BNPL, card payments, and bank transfers, before deduction of platform fees and before VAT removal.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Gross platform settlements cannot be netted against Stripe transaction fees or Affirm discount charges; such fees are deductible only as operating expenses with documentary evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 — Cost of Sales and Deductible Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, customs duties, logistics, warehousing, marketing, platform commissions, chargeback and refund reserves, salaries, and administrative overheads supported by ordinary commercial documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to overseas affiliates or suppliers require transfer-pricing documentation; undocumented management fees to the non-resident shareholder are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary reconciliation items: disallowed fines, non-deductible entertainment, thin-capitalisation interest limitation (interest exceeding 30% of EBITDA), depreciation additions and recapture, and the statutory donation cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest on shareholder loans is exposed to the 30% EBITDA cap; withholding taxes creditable in the LLC's name are recorded separately in Box 10.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of unused losses generated within the preceding 5 tax years; no carry-back exists.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of the Egyptian LLC remain usable after a share transfer, but the annual offset cannot exceed the current-year taxable base and ownership-change scrutiny may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciled taxable base after exemptions, incentive deductions, and loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the LLC is a domestic-risk online reseller with no foreign permanent establishment, the full Egyptian-source profit is taxable at 22.5%; no unilateral deduction is allowed for imputed inter-company charges absent substantiation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Product of the net taxable income and the 22.5% statutory rate, before instalment and withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No tax is computed here on behalf of the non-resident shareholder; dividend or royalty withholding is handled by the payer's separate withholding declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly instalments, employees' payroll tax remittances, VAT-borne input credits where recoverable, prior-year overpayments, and withholding tax suffered in Egypt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits must be traceable to deposit receipts in the LLC's tax file; a parent company cannot claim credits for taxes paid on behalf of the LLC without a formal set-off ruling from the ETA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 — Net Tax Payable / Refund Claim
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance due to the ETA or refundable to the LLC; payment may be made by bank transfer or ETA-approved electronic channel.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The balance must be funded from the LLC's own resources before the 4-month deadline; a non-resident shareholder cannot substitute shareholder loans for the corporate tax settlement without triggering thin-capitalisation review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature of the LLC manager, the appointed certified accountant, and the external auditor attesting accuracy and completeness of the return and accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign director who signs the e-filed return assumes criminal exposure; a local licensed tax agent may file under a power of attorney, but the manager remains the responsible person before Egyptian courts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative fine of 5% of the assessed tax for each month or part of a month (minimum EGP 500 per month) under the Unified Tax Procedures Law (Law No. 15 of 2021), plus a monthly arrears surcharge on unpaid tax; intentional non-filing or concealment exposes the manager to imprisonment from 6 months to 5 years and fines reaching EGP 10,000,000 under the tax-evasion chapter, with the ETA authorised to freeze bank accounts, suspend tax clearance, and order a travel ban.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly Advance Tax Instalment Slip — ETA e-filing portal (payment module attached to Form No. 20 annual reconciliation).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly instalment payments during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Each instalment is due by the end of the first month of each quarter; the annual return reconciles the four instalments with the final assessed tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as a percentage of the prior-year assessed tax or a justified forecast of the current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Instalments paid by the LLC are creditable in Box 10 of Form 20; under-payment exposes the investment to a 3%-per-month surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique digital receipt code generated by the ETA portal for each wire transfer or card payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments must be executed from the LLC's Egyptian bank account; payment made by a foreign parent is treated as a separate financing transaction requiring documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to pay each instalment attracts a monthly surcharge on the outstanding amount; the ETA may attach bank deposits and impose a temporary freeze on the LLC's import/export activity until arrears are cleared.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends actually distributed to non-resident shareholders (Article 67, Law No. 91 of 2005); no withholding applies to distributions to resident juridical persons meeting the Egyptian participation exemption conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To benefit from an income-tax treaty, the non-resident beneficial owner must deliver to the LLC before the distribution date: (i) a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority and valid for the year of distribution, (ii) a Beneficial Ownership Statement confirming the recipient has no Egyptian permanent establishment, and (iii) the ETA's advance ruling on the reduced withholding rate, filed through the ETA protocol on non-resident remittances. Where advance approval is not secured, the LLC must withhold at the statutory 10% and the beneficial owner may file a refund claim with the ETA within 5 years of the distribution date.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT for non-resident recipients: 20% on royalties, technical and management fees (Article 68, Law No. 91 of 2005) and 20% on interest paid on shareholder or related-party loans (Article 69, subject to the 30% EBITDA interest-limitation rule). Treaty rates generally range from 10% to 15%; some Egyptian DTAs grant 5% or 0% for qualifying corporate shareholders and government entities. Relief is conditional on the TRC, beneficial ownership, and absence of a permanent establishment in Egypt.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when the aggregate value of related-party transactions in the fiscal year exceeds EGP 8,000,000; Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required when the multinational group's consolidated revenue reaches or exceeds EGP 2,000,000,000 (approximately USD 41,000,000), with the CbCR notification filed via the ETA portal.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has no standalone Economic Substances Regulation statute comparable to the UAE ESR, but the ETA applies a functional economic-substance review under the beneficial-ownership clause of DTAs, the management-and-control test for residence, and the general anti-abuse rules of Law No. 91 of 2005. A portable-power e-commerce LLC must demonstrate genuine presence in Egypt: physical warehouse or fulfillment capacity, personnel exercising procurement and marketing decisions, board minutes held or documented in Egypt, inventory risk, and a rational transfer-pricing profile. A mail-box entity whose online-sales profits are attributed to a foreign parent without local substance will be re-denominated as an Egyptian resident or as having an Egyptian permanent establishment, with full CIT and surcharges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Reporting only bank-card settlements while concealing Stripe payouts or Affirm BNPL instalments; booking refunds without valid credit notes; splitting retailer turnover among shell bank accounts; or inflating the cost of goods through fabricated purchase invoices for imported solar panels.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment from 6 months to 5 years plus fine of EGP 100,000 to EGP 10,000,000 under Law No. 19 of 2016 read with Law No. 15 of 2021; the tax due is recovered with a surcharge of up to 5 times the evaded amount; digital payment records are judicially seized from payment platforms.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The LLC manager and any director who signed the false declaration face criminal prosecution; the corporate veil is pierced where deducted-but-unremitted withholding taxes are involved; courts order civil restitution of the evaded tax, interest, and fines, and approve travel bans and asset freezes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the LLC as a letter-box: no Egyptian employees, no warehouse, all commercial decisions taken abroad, and sales income technically booked by a foreign parent while the LLC serves only as a routing entity for solar products in the Suez Canal zone.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the offshore parent as an Egyptian permanent establishment under Article 32 of Law No. 91 of 2005; assessment of 22.5% CIT on the attributable sales profit, monthly surcharges, and denial of treaty benefits under the beneficial-ownership clause; the tax card and import-export code may be suspended.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who legalised the deceptive Egyptian arrangements are jointly and severally liable for the re-assessed PE tax and late-payment surcharges; repeated violations result in criminal fines and a ban on founding or managing companies in Egypt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling solar portable power units to the foreign parent below the resale-price benchmark, purchasing components from a related Hong Kong or Gulf trader above the CUP benchmark to strip Egyptian margin, or failing to prepare the Local File when controlled transactions exceed EGP 8,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA transfer-pricing adjustment restores the arm's-length margin, disallows the excess cost, and computes additional tax plus a monthly arrears surcharge; failure to file documentation carries fines under Law No. 15 of 2021 of between EGP 500 and EGP 1,000,000; the assessment remains open beyond the standard statute of limitations where concealment is shown.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The transfer-pricing policy documentation is signed by the director; knowingly false documentation constitutes criminal false declaration; civil liability extends to the adjusted tax, penalties, and the parent's indemnity claim in liquidation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the BNPL and card rails to absorb retail payments without payment-source surveillance, holding Stripe payouts in a foreign personal account, settling merchant cash from undisclosed third-party accounts, or failing to maintain beneficial-ownership records for investors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under Law No. 80 of 2002 (Anti-Money Laundering Law): administrative fines up to EGP 5,000,000 and imprisonment between 3 months and 7 years; the ETA may revoke the tax clearance certificate, and the banking regulator can suspend merchant-payment processing in Egypt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The compliance officer and managing director face personal fines and imprisonment for failing to report suspicious online-retail flows; travel bans are available in money-laundering investigations, and courts may pierce the veil where directors commingle retail proceeds with personal accounts.
